clue.text: Spirited sort of writer ?

parts.note: a spirit, or someone who writes books that appear under another person's name; 'Spirited' plays on both

explanation.surface: A lively, vivacious kind of author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirited' looks like 'lively', but it means 'made of spirit': a phantom, and also the kind of writer who works unseen under someone else's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A phantom is a spirit, and an uncredited author paid to write someone's memoir is called a ghost writer.

clue.text: Port wine tip

parts.note: Graves is a Bordeaux wine
an end is a tip

explanation.surface: A hint about which fortified wine to choose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the wine; it is a harbour town, on the Thames estuary in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravesend is a harbour town on the Thames estuary in Kent.

clue.text: Basket-maker gets fresh rise after start of October

indicators.note: the shuffled letters come after the first piece
the start of a word is its first letter
fresh means new, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A basket-weaver gets a new pay rise from October.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' turns RISE into SIER, placed 'after' O, the first letter of October.
explanation.definitionFit: A willow whose pliable shoots are woven into baskets makes baskets in a sense: wickerwork comes from it.

clue.text: They draw up with a vehicle — different sort

indicators.note: in a down entry 'up' means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a cart is a vehicle

indicators.note: different means the letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Drivers pull up in a car of a different make.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses CART into TRAC, and 'different' makes TORS from SORT. 'draw up' seems one phrase but is split.
explanation.definitionFit: Tractors are farm vehicles that pull ploughs and trailers, so they draw loads.

clue.text: Flier shot by another

parts.note: the nursery rhyme bird killed by the sparrow's bow and arrow

explanation.surface: An aviator brought down by a fellow pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme 'Who killed Cock Robin?' answers 'I, said the Sparrow, with my bow and arrow': one bird shot by another.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme the sparrow shoots this bird with an arrow, so it is a flier shot by another flier.

clue.text: Wind one found in a pass

indicators.note: the numeral is placed inside the word for a pass

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A gust met at a mountain pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' reads as breeze, but it is the verb to wind, rhyming with 'find'.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind something is to twist it round in loops, as a coil does.

clue.text: Set pieces for précis-writers ?

definitions.meaning: components in a radio set that store electrical charge
people who shorten text into summaries

explanation.surface: Set pieces prepared for summary writers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set pieces' suggests a rehearsed routine; here a set is a wireless, and its capacitors were once called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Capacitors in a radio set were once called by this name, and précis-writers shorten text into summaries.

clue.text: One causing friction at the stationer's

definitions.text: One causing friction at the stationer's

parts.words: One causing friction at the stationer's
parts.note: an eraser bought at a stationer's works by being rubbed on paper

explanation.surface: A troublemaker in the stationery shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causing friction' suggests stirring up trouble; it is literal, an eraser rubbed on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A pencil eraser is called by this name in Britain, and it removes marks by being rubbed on paper.

clue.text: Very bright fish-a tin variety

parts.note: brill is a flatfish

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the letters take another arrangement

explanation.surface: A dazzling assortment of tinned fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' rearranges A TIN into IANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Brilliant means dazzling, shining intensely.

clue.text: Marked the refusal of Edward's proposal

parts.note: no is a refusal
Ted is short for Edward

explanation.surface: A rejected marriage proposal is remembered.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as Edward's proposal being refused; the parts are NO and TED.
explanation.definitionFit: Noted means observed or remarked, as marked does in 'he marked the change'.

clue.text: Liveliness I aim to stir vp in a girl

indicators.note: the stirred letters are placed inside the girl's name

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

indicators.note: to stir up is to agitate, so the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone means to get a young woman excited and lively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir up' scrambles I AIM TO into IMATIO, which goes inside ANN (the girl; the 'a' before it is a link).
explanation.definitionFit: Animation is vivacity or spiritedness, the quality of being full of life.

clue.text: Made only about one pound

indicators.note: the word for 'only' is put around the other pieces

parts.note: but means only, as in 'but a child'
I is the Roman numeral one
L is the abbreviation for pound (libra)

explanation.surface: Earned barely a single pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts BUT round I and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Built is a past tense of construct, so it can stand for made in 'they made a house'.

clue.text: Mistakes of a sailor concerning going astern

indicators.note: a ship going astern moves backwards, so the run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
re means concerning, about

explanation.surface: A sailor's blunders while reversing his vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going astern' reverses the whole run A TAR RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are errors listed for correction in a printed book.

clue.text: Showed meat in animal brought back

indicators.note: the meat is placed inside the reversed animal
brought back means the animal's name is turned round

parts.note: a deer is an animal
veal is calf meat

explanation.surface: A butcher displayed meat inside a carcass returned to the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns DEER into REED, and 'in' puts VEAL inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Revealed means disclosed or exposed to view, as showed does.

clue.text: Dangerous drops in prices including rise of Eastern currency

indicators.note: the word prices holds the reversed currency inside
in a down entry a rise reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: pice was a small Indian coin

explanation.surface: Prices fall sharply as an Asian currency strengthens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise of' reverses PICE into ECIP, and 'including' puts it inside PRICES. 'drops' looks like a fall in prices but means cliffs.
explanation.definitionFit: Precipices are sheer cliff faces with perilous falls.

clue.text: Undertaking to chop the right pine-trees

indicators.note: to chop things up is to cut and mix them, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A forestry project to fell the correct pines.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text has a stray '..' that the page does not print. 'chop' rearranges R plus PINETREES; 'Undertaking' looks like the verb of the surface, but it is a noun meaning a venture.
explanation.definitionFit: An enterprise is a project or venture taken on, a bold piece of business.

clue.text: Experimental shelter — one a vet built

parts.note: a tent is a shelter

indicators.note: built means assembled from parts, so the letters are put together anew

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A temporary shelter built by a vet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'built' rearranges I A VET into ATIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tentative means provisional or trial, not yet settled.

clue.text: Charles, the young skipper ?

definitions.meaning: Charles ..., the English essayist of 'Essays of Elia'
a baby sheep, which skips about in spring fields

explanation.surface: Charles, the boy captain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skipper' suggests a ship's captain; here it is an animal that skips.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lamb was a Romantic essayist, and a young sheep frisking in a field is a skipper in the playful sense.

clue.text: Labour stateswoman has agreement on land

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece sits on top of the other

parts.note: a bond is a binding agreement
a field is a piece of land

explanation.surface: A Labour politician has a deal on some land.
explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Bondfield was the first woman British cabinet minister, Labour's Minister of Labour in 1929.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Bondfield was a Labour MP and Britain's first woman cabinet minister.

clue.text: Writer misrepresented Marne battle

parts.note: ink is what does the writing on the page

indicators.note: misrepresented means shown in a false form, so the letters are distorted

explanation.surface: An author gave a false account of the Marne fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misrepresented' rearranges MARNE into ERMAN. 'Marne battle' seems one phrase, but Marne is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Inkerman was an 1854 Crimean War battle near Sevastopol.

clue.text: Lear character had a shiny nose

definitions.text: Lear character had a shiny nose

parts.words: Lear character had a shiny nose
parts.note: Edward Lear's nonsense poem about a creature 'with a Luminous Nose'

explanation.surface: A figure in Shakespeare's King Lear had a glowing nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lear' suggests Shakespeare's king, but it is Edward Lear, the nonsense poet, whose poem 'The Dong with a Luminous Nose' names this creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Lear wrote a nonsense poem about a wandering creature whose nose glowed like a lamp.

clue.text: In part of London many telephone to a Lancs town

indicators.note: the other pieces go in the London district's name

parts.note: Acton is a district of west London
C is the Roman numeral 100, standing for many
to ring is to telephone

explanation.surface: Someone in London makes many calls to a town in Lancashire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts C and RING inside ACTON. Lancs is short for Lancashire, a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Accrington is a mill town in Lancashire, in north-west England.

clue.text: Conrad's novel opportunity

explanation.surface: A Joseph Conrad book offers something new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like 'new', as in a novel opportunity; it is a book title.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Conrad wrote a 1913 novel of this title, and an opportunity is a favourable opening.

clue.text: Lady traveller in Chesterfield ?

definitions.meaning: Lady Hester, the English explorer of the Middle East
Philip, 4th Earl of Chesterfield, author of the 'Letters to His Son', bore this family name

explanation.surface: A woman journeying through the Derbyshire town of Chesterfield.
explanation.walkthrough: Chesterfield is a town in Derbyshire, but here it is the Earl, whose surname matched that of Lady Hester the traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Hester Stanhope travelled through the Levant, and the Earl of Chesterfield's family name was the same.

clue.text: Attempts by gunmen

explanation.surface: Gunmen make attempts.
explanation.definitionFit: A try is called a shot, and a marksman is described as a good shot.

clue.text: Start by cancelling court fixture ?

definitions.meaning: to begin a journey, to depart
a tennis set that is called off

explanation.surface: Getting going by calling off a tennis match.
explanation.walkthrough: A set is a unit of play on a tennis court, and something 'off' is cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off is to depart or begin; read as a tennis set that is off, it is a cancelled game.

clue.text: Marxian view of people's religion

parts.note: Marx called religion a drug that dulls the masses

explanation.surface: What Marx thought of popular faith.
explanation.walkthrough: Karl Marx wrote that religion 'is the opium of the people'.
explanation.definitionFit: Marx wrote that religion is the drug of the masses, naming this narcotic.

clue.text: A man, in the final analysis

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words final analysis

explanation.surface: A person, when all is said and done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the final analysis' reads as 'ultimately'; the name runs across the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan is a man's name.

clue.text: Hunter of French black duck returns

indicators.note: returns means the run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: noir is French for black
O is a duck, a score of nothing in cricket

explanation.surface: A hunter of a dark French duck heads back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' reverses NOIR plus O.
explanation.definitionFit: Orion is the giant huntsman of Greek myth, now a constellation.

clue.text: Flower of pantomime

parts.note: a garden plant that shares its name with Harlequin's sweetheart in the harlequinade

explanation.surface: The finest of Christmas pantomime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower of' looks like 'the best of'; it is a real flower, and the same name belongs to the girl in the old pantomime harlequinade.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquilegia is a garden plant also called by this name, which is also Harlequin's sweetheart in the harlequinade.

clue.text: Writer figures on getting round tedious opening

indicators.note: the figures go round the opening letter

parts.note: sevens are figures, numbers

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An author, keen on figures, gets past a dull introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting round' puts SEVENS round T, the first letter of 'tedious', with ON after.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson was the Scottish author of Treasure Island.

clue.text: Called for return of foreign island

indicators.note: return means the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: de is the French for 'of', a foreign 'of'
the Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: Someone is summoned to come back from an overseas island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses DE plus MAN. 'Called' looks like 'summoned'; here it means given a name.
explanation.definitionFit: To be named is to be called by a given name.
